new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement about word stress exists. The only first-hand linguistic source says Chomo (= the Ladhu/Como half of Como Karim) is a tone language with three level tones, like Proto-Jukunoid; nothing is said about stress or accent in any snippet returned for any Shimizu/Chomo/Jukunoid + stress/accent query.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone inventory statement only; based on Shimizu's own Chomo (Dhu) data elicited from Shomo speakers at Gindin Dorawa (near Wukari), plus a 'Karm' list in vol. 2. Snippet-view only: page number for the tone statement could not be recovered; the book is print-only (HathiTrust search-only, could not be reached by automated download).
new_statements.identity_note: Como Karim [cfg] / como1258 covers two groups: the Chomo/Shomo, self-name Ladhu (/là-dhu/, language /nu à dhu/), south of Karim, and the Karim/Karinjo, self-name Kiyu (Khiyiu), at Karim Lamido (Ethnologue treats Karim = Kirim, Kiyu as a dialect; no separate glottocode). Shimizu 1980, the only linguistic source, describes Chomo (Dhu) from Shomo speakers elicited at Gindin Dorawa near Wukari and states only that 'the Karim reported by Meek is closely related to Chomo'; his vol. 2 sets also carry a 'Karm' column. The three-level-tone statement therefore applies to Chomo (Ladhu), not demonstrably to Kiyu.
